## Key Insights

1. Summer Sowing Status: As on March 17, 2025, the area sown under summer crops is 41.28 lakh ha as compared to 37.55 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.  Of this, area of 28.24 lakh ha has been sown under rice this year against the previous year area of 25.14 lakh ha (increase of 3.10 lakh ha).
2. Rabi harvesting Status: As on 13.03.2025, 25.02% of area has been harvested all over India. Approximately 44.00% area of Pulses mainly in Lathyrus (77%), Urdbean (77%), Kulthi (61%), Moongbean (54%); 44.30% area of Shri Anna & Coarse Cereals mainly in Jowar (74%); 38.33% area  of  Oilseeds  majorly  in  Rapeseed  &  Mustard  (26%);  and  21.38%  area  of  Rice  has  been harvested for Rabi crops 2024-25.
3. Rabi Season Area Coverage : For Rabi horticulture crops ,  major producing states report the following sowing areas: Onion - 10.44 lakh ha (9.21 lakh ha last year), Potato - 19.93 lakh ha (19.56 lakh ha last year), Tomato - 2.49 lakh ha (2.59 lakh ha last year).

## 4. Weather Update :

- a) Temperature: A  gradual  rise  in  maximum  temperatures  by  about  2-4°C  is  expected  over Northwest  India  in  the  next  4-5  days.  However,  no  significant  change  in  maximum temperatures is expected over Central India in the next 24 hours, followed by a drop of 24°C over the subsequent 3-4 days.  East India is likely to experience stable temperatures for the next 48 hours, after which a decline of 2-3°C is expected over the next three days. the rest of India is not expected to witness any major fluctuations in maximum temperatures during the next 3-4 days.
- b) Rainfall Distribution: From Mar 01- 12 Mar, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 34% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: -61%; (ii) Northwest India: -19%; (iii) Central India: -99%; and South Peninsula: +20%
3.  A  fresh Western  Disturbance seen  as  a  cyclonic  circulation  over  West  Iran  & neighbourhood in lower to upper tropospheric levels. It is likely to move gradually eastwards  and  impact States  of  Western  Himalayan  region during  next  10-12th March.
4.  Overall, rainfall is likely to be above normal over south Peninsular India & adjoining central India and below normal over rest parts of the country during the week.

## 5. Inputs Situation

- a) Water Reservoir Status : As of March 13, 2025, the live storage in 155 major reservoirs is 85.373 BCM (47% of total capacity). Storage is at 119% of last year's level and 116% of the 10-year average. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
- b) Groundwater Levels : Approximately 66.6% of monitoring wells show water levels between 05 m, while 29.1% report levels between 5-10 m. Decadal analysis (2014-2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024.

## Temperature Forecast

13 th  Mar - 19 th  Mar 2025

- a) No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over plains of Northwest India during next 24 hours and fall by 2-3°C thereafter.
- b) No significant change in maximum temperatures likely over central India during next 2 days and fall by 2-3°C thereafter.
- c) Gradual fall in maximum temperatures by 2-4°C likely over many parts of West India during the week.
- d) Gradual rise in maximum temperatures by about 2-3°C likely over East India during 1st half of the week and no significant change thereafter.

- e) Gradual rise in maximum temperatures by about 2-4°C likely over many parts of south peninsular India during the week.

## 20 th  Mar - 26 th  Mar, 2025

- f) Maximum  temperatures  are  likely  to  be  above  normal  by  2-4°C  over  most  parts  of northwest India and by 2-3°C over most parts of East India; near normal over Gujarat and parts of northeast India.
- g) There is low to moderate probability of heat wave conditions over south Rajasthan,Gujarat and Odisha during some days of the week.
- h) Minimum temperatures are likely to be below normal or near normal over most parts of the country.

Key Insights

1. Summer Sowing Status: As on March 17, 2025, the area sown under summer crops is 41.28 lakh ha as compared to 37.55 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.  Of this, area of 28.24 lakh ha has been sown under rice this year against the previous year area of 25.14 lakh ha (increase of 3.10 lakh ha).
2. Rabi harvesting Status: As on 13.03.2025, 25.02% of area has been harvested all over India. Approximately 44.00% area of Pulses mainly in Lathyrus (77%), Urdbean (77%), Kulthi (61%), Moongbean (54%); 44.30% area of Shri Anna & Coarse Cereals mainly in Jowar (74%); 38.33% area  of  Oilseeds  majorly  in  Rapeseed  &  Mustard  (26%);  and  21.38%  area  of  Rice  has  been harvested for Rabi crops 2024-25.
3. Rabi Season Area Coverage : For Rabi horticulture crops ,  major producing states report the following sowing areas: Onion - 10.44 lakh ha (9.21 lakh ha last year), Potato - 19.93 lakh ha (19.56 lakh ha last year), Tomato - 2.49 lakh ha (2.59 lakh ha last year).

4. Weather Update :

- a) Temperature: A  gradual  rise  in  maximum  temperatures  by  about  2-4°C  is  expected  over Northwest  India  in  the  next  4-5  days.  However,  no  significant  change  in  maximum temperatures is expected over Central India in the next 24 hours, followed by a drop of 24°C over the subsequent 3-4 days.  East India is likely to experience stable temperatures for the next 48 hours, after which a decline of 2-3°C is expected over the next three days. the rest of India is not expected to witness any major fluctuations in maximum temperatures during the next 3-4 days.
- b) Rainfall Distribution: From Mar 01- 12 Mar, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 34% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: -61%; (ii) Northwest India: -19%; (iii) Central India: -99%; and South Peninsula: +20%
3.  A  fresh Western  Disturbance seen  as  a  cyclonic  circulation  over  West  Iran  & neighbourhood in lower to upper tropospheric levels. It is likely to move gradually eastwards  and  impact States  of  Western  Himalayan  region during  next  10-12th March.
4.  Overall, rainfall is likely to be above normal over south Peninsular India & adjoining central India and below normal over rest parts of the country during the week.

5. Inputs Situation

- a) Water Reservoir Status : As of March 13, 2025, the live storage in 155 major reservoirs is 85.373 BCM (47% of total capacity). Storage is at 119% of last year's level and 116% of the 10-year average. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
- b) Groundwater Levels : Approximately 66.6% of monitoring wells show water levels between 05 m, while 29.1% report levels between 5-10 m. Decadal analysis (2014-2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024.

Key Insights

1. Summer Sowing Status: As on March 17, 2025, the area sown under summer crops is 41.28 lakh ha as compared to 37.55 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year. Of this, area of 28.24 lakh ha has been sown under rice this year against the previous year area of 25.14 lakh ha (increase of 3.10 lakh ha). 2. Rabi harvesting Status: As on 13.03.2025, 25.02% of area has been harvested all over India. Approximately 44.00% area of Pulses mainly in Lathyrus (77%), Urdbean (77%), Kulthi (61%), Moongbean (54%); 44.30% area of Shri Anna & Coarse Cereals mainly in Jowar (74%); 38.33% area of Oilseeds majorly in Rapeseed & Mustard (26%); and 21.38% area of Rice has been harvested for Rabi crops 2024-25. 3. Rabi Season Area Coverage: For Rabi horticulture crops, major producing states report the following sowing areas: Onion – 10.44 lakh ha (9.21 lakh ha last year), Potato – 19.93 lakh ha (19.56 lakh ha last year), Tomato – 2.49 lakh ha (2.59 lakh ha last year). 4. Weather Update: a) Temperature: A gradual rise in maximum temperatures by about 2-4°C is expected over Northwest India in the next 4-5 days. However, no significant change in maximum temperatures is expected over Central India in the next 24 hours, followed by a drop of 2- 4°C over the subsequent 3-4 days. East India is likely to experience stable temperatures for the next 48 hours, after which a decline of 2-3°C is expected over the next three days. the rest of India is not expected to witness any major fluctuations in maximum temperatures during the next 3-4 days. b) Rainfall Distribution: From Mar 01– 12 Mar, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 34% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: -61%; (ii) Northwest India: -19%; (iii) Central India: -99%; and South Peninsula: +20%  A fresh Western Disturbance seen as a cyclonic circulation over West Iran & neighbourhood in lower to upper tropospheric levels. It is likely to move gradually eastwards and impact States of Western Himalayan region during next 10-12th March.  Overall, rainfall is likely to be above normal over south Peninsular India & adjoining central India and below normal over rest parts of the country during the week. 5. Inputs Situation a) Water Reservoir Status: As of March 13, 2025, the live storage in 155 major reservoirs is 85.373 BCM (47% of total capacity). Storage is at 119% of last year’s level and 116% of the 10-year average. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period. b) Groundwater Levels: Approximately 66.6% of monitoring wells show water levels between 0- 5 m, while 29.1% report levels between 5-10 m. Decadal analysis (2014–2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024.
